alex_sales: Quick sync - Borealis POC. They hit a blocker around long-lived sessions + SSO. Can someone confirm whether our SDK supports session resumption with short-lived creds?

maya_se: We do ephemeral creds via the SDK but session resumption across websocket reconnects is still a bit manual. You can persist the connection token + v1 resume token.

tom_eng: Confirming — runtime issues only if client reinitializes a new socket without resume token. We have a sample: `client.resume(session_token)` in the JS SDK.

alex_sales: Ok thanks. The customer wants automatic refresh without a full re-auth flow (Okta SSO). Any example?

maya_se: For Okta you can mint an ephemeral API key via backend exchange (short-lived). Pattern: user does SSO -> backend calls IdP -> backend calls Redwood to create ephemeral key -> return to client. On reconnect, client calls backend to get refreshed ephemeral then calls `client.resume(...)` with the new token.

leah_security: A note for SOC2 crowd: persistence of resume tokens counts as secrets. Recommend storing them in encrypted session store and rotate on logout. Also: advise customers to set TTL <= 1h for ephemeral tokens.

alex_sales: Borealis asking about pricing impact of session-resume/long-lived streams vs frequent reconnects. Any numbers?

maya_se: Rough: continuous stream with resume uses fewer auth handshakes and avoids re-creating KV cache; tokens don't change cost — cost is per token generated. But reconnects cause repeated model context warmups which drive up token consumption + latency. If they keep the same session for N requests, cost reduces by ~15-30% depending on batch behavior.

tom_eng: Also note: if they use prefix caching + resume we preserve KV cache — big saving on long conversations. If they're doing short queries (1-2 turns) reconnecting is fine.

alex_sales: They also submitted the security questionnaire: Q on KMS and offline key rotation. leah, can you paste the recommended config?

leah_security: Paste: ```
- Use customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) for Private deployment
- Rotate data keys monthly, rotate master keys per your policy
- Enable HSM for highest assurance (via Redwood Private)
- Audit logs: enable S3 export + enable CloudTrail/Stackdriver forwarding
```

alex_sales: Perfect. One more: they want structured output + tool calls (JSON schema) and worry about schema drift when we failover to a fallback model. How do we guarantee compatibility?

maya_se: We recommend pinned model versions for the POC (e.g., redwood-2.1.0) + fallback mapping rules. Also add a post-processing validation step that rejects out-of-spec outputs. SDK supports `validateSchema(schema)` helper that returns structured errors.

tom_eng: For streaming structured toolcall flows, include a final confirm step where the last token is a compact checksum of the payload so caller can detect truncation. Example: `checksum(payload) -> call confirm_tool(checksum...)`

alex_sales: Action items: 1) Maya: send the Okta ephemeral flow sample and small JS snippet. 2) Tom: provide numbers for cost delta reconnect vs resume (ballpark). 3) Leah: paste the KMS/HSM config into the questionnaire. 4) I'll schedule follow-up demo on Thursday.
